headline: Margins compress and dividend axed amid restructuring plan
summary_short: Dentsply Sirona posted Q1 FY2026 revenue of $880M (+0.1% y/y, -8.4% q/q) and swung to a $10M net loss from $20M of net income a year ago, as gross margin fell 450bps to 48.5% on $67M of restructuring charges tied to a new cost-cutting plan and the Board eliminated the quarterly dividend.
summary_long: Revenue was roughly flat y/y at $880M as EDS price/APAC growth offset lower EDS/OIS/imaging volumes in the Americas and EMEA and the Byte exit. Gross margin fell to 48.5% from 53.0% on lower volumes, tariffs, unfavorable mix, and the Byte exit, partly offset by FX. The company recorded $67M of restructuring costs under its new February 2026 plan ($120M targeted annualized savings), driving a $35M operating loss (from $63M income) and a $10M net loss (from $20M income) a year earlier. Operating cash flow rose to $40M from $7M. The board eliminated the quarterly dividend and made no buybacks; cash fell to $190M as debt was repaid. FY2026 capex guidance: $125M-$150M.

drivers.explanation: Reported net sales were roughly flat y/y as favorable FX offset a constant-currency decline from lower EDS/OIS volumes in the Americas/EMEA and the Byte exit, partly offset by APAC growth and EDS pricing.
Margin fell 450bps to 48.5%, driven by lower EDS/OIS volumes and imaging products in the Americas, the Byte exit, higher tariff costs, and unfavorable mix, partly offset by a favorable FX benefit.
Rose 9.7% y/y in line with the gross-margin decline; reflects the same higher tariff costs and unfavorable product mix cited as gross-profit drivers.
Swung to a $35M loss from $63M of income, driven by the gross-margin decline plus $67M of restructuring and other costs under the new 2026 Plan, up from $9M a year earlier.

Increase of $33M y/y was primarily driven by lower accounts receivable and prepaid/other current assets, partially offset by higher inventories and lower accrued liabilities.
Increase of $33M y/y reflects supply chain equipment upgrades, capacity expansion, DS Core enhancements, and the new global ERP system; company guides full-year 2026 capex to $125M-$150M.
Cash fell $136M during the quarter as $53M of investing outflows (capex, hedge settlement) and $119M of financing outflows (debt repayments) exceeded $40M of operating cash flow.
Sequential decline reflects a February 2026 repayment in full of EUR26 million of private placement notes at maturity, plus other scheduled long-term debt repayments.
Sequentially flat; the y/y decline reflects the prior year's larger current debt balance from since-repaid short-term borrowings and the 364-day bridge loan drawn in Q1 2025.
Decline reflects the $10M net loss plus unfavorable other comprehensive items (currency translation), with no offsetting buybacks or dividends paid this quarter.
Essentially unchanged y/y; the company made no share repurchases during the quarter.

Q1 FY2026 results were pressured by tariff costs, unfavorable mix, and the Byte exit, prompting a new Board-approved restructuring plan (targeting $120M of annualized savings) and elimination of the quarterly dividend.
